page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, consisting of 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 64 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng, placing in the top 25 percent of tested instances. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and memory bandwidth tests fall within the average range. A notable performance bottleneck is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-model LLM prompt processing, both of which rank in the bottom 25 percent.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, this server type provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive multi-threaded processing or local storage. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive web serving, but less efficient for heavy multi-threaded decompression or large-scale machine learning inference.
